title: Query count of the majority continuation tree
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $C$ be a set of available coordinates among $n$ coordinates, and let $a,b\in\{−1,1\}$. For any decision tree $T$ using coordinates in $C$ and any sign-valued input $x\in\{−1,1\}^{n}$, the continuation tree that stops when $a=b$ and otherwise runs $T$ makes zero queries if $a=b$, and makes exactly as many queries as $T$ does on $x$ if $a\ne b$.
hypotheses_covered: set of available coordinates $C$ among the $n$ coordinates
